key_insight: High-pressure torsion turns TiZrHfNbTa into a nanostructured, defect-rich alloy where electrons carry most heat, while phonon transport is strongly suppressed by dislocations and grain boundaries.
engineering_relevance: The results show how severe plastic deformation can tune thermal and electrical transport in refractory HEAs, which is useful for designing robust materials for high-temperature and energy-related applications.
method: Equiatomic TiZrHfNbTa was processed by high-pressure torsion (HPT).
Microstructure evolution included dislocation accumulation, ~40 nm grains, and partial BCC-to-omega transformation.
Thermal/electrical transport was interpreted with the Wiedemann-Franz law to separate electron and phonon contributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a non-monotonic specific heat and thermal conductivity response with strain, while electrical conductivity decreases monotonically to a steady state; phonons contribute only about 11–23% of thermal transport.
watch_item: The transport interpretation depends on assumptions in the Wiedemann-Franz separation, so phase heterogeneity and defect evolution should be considered when generalizing to other HEAs or processing routes.
paper_title: Thermal and electrical conductivity of a refractory high-entropy alloy after high-pressure torsion: Electron versus phonon contributions
